title: POLYGON BASICS FULL EXPLANATION IN 10 MINUTES
description:
"voice  in this video generated by AI".

Best way to say it:

👉 “A polygon has no maximum limit on the number of sides.”
👉 Or
👉 “Number of sides can increase indefinitely (approach infinity).”

🔶 Why not infinity?

If sides become truly infinite → it becomes a circle, not a polygon 

A polygon must have countable straight sides



Interior & Exterior Angles of Polygons  | Full Explanation + Diagrams    Polygon Angles
 Learn Interior & Exterior Angles of Polygons in the simplest way!

In this video, we explain both concepts clearly with easy diagrams and examples.

🟢 What is an Interior Angle?
🔵 What is an Exterior Angle?
🔁 Relationship: Interior + Exterior = 180°
📌 Important Formulas:
✔ Sum of Interior Angles = (n − 2) × 180°
✔ Sum of Exterior Angles = 360°

🎯 Example:
Hexagon (6 sides)
Interior sum = 720°
Exterior sum = 360°

🧠 Easy Trick:
Interior = Inside
Exterior = Outside

👉 This video is perfect for:
✔ School students
✔ Beginners in Geometry
✔ Competitive exam preparation

interior angles, exterior angles, polygons, geometry basics, polygon formulas, math tricks, learn geometry, easy math

asr.full_text: Lets unpack this, what is the basic rules to call a shape formal polygon. There are certain rules to call a shape a polygon. First lets see about the term E polygon In Greek Poly means many and Gon means angles right? Yes correct! Gon means the angles or angles To become a Polygon.. There are two strict rules First .. It must be completely closed and of 2D shape That means , no place or small gap should be there Exactly The shape to be inside should be closed so that it cannot come out And the next rule is It must be formed only with straight lines these are also known as Edges Another thing is, to create a polygon, it should have at least three sides. Yes, if we think logically, we cannot close any shape with two lines, right? One side is open. Right. To close that, we definitely need that third line. So, we call the polygon that closes with those three sides as a triangle. Hmm, triangle, okay. But I have a doubt here. What is that condition? If a triangle is formed, the total number of small sides that are added to these three sides should always be greater than the size of the third side. Hmm, got it. Let's imagine this as a piece of wood or a fence. Let's place a six-foot-sized stone on the ground and connect two-foot and three-foot-sized stones to it. Right how about the polygon family on top? That family is very interesting. If there are 4 sides, they are called quadrilaterals. Rectangles, squares, everything comes in it. If there are 5 sides, it is called a pentagon. What if there are 6 sides? We call it a hexagon, right? I immediately remember the honey bee nest. Yes, honeycomb is the best example of a hexagon. The hexagons with 6 sides, they are all octagon shapes. There is one more interesting point in our source. Oh what is that? The shape of 9 sides is called nonagon or enagon. Now if there are 10 sides, they are called decagon. Wait wait, how many sides can a polygon have? Does it have a maximum limit? What's fascinating here is, This changes the perception. Okay, but not just by the number of sides, how do you divide the polygons? Sides can be divided by America. First, regular polygon and then irregular polygon. Hmm. If it is regular, would all be equal? Yes. If the sides in the shape are definitely of equal size and the inner angles are equal, that is a regular polygon. Like a perfect square. Convex polygon and concave polygon. What is convex? Angles within the shape are convex if they are less than 180 degrees. But if one angle is more than 180 of this angle is formed inside the shape. There is a formula to find out the amount of the interior angle if we combine all these interior angles. n-2 x 180 degrees Wait, wait. n-2 x 180. Here n is the number of sides, right? Yes. But, why do we have to subtract 2 from n without multiplying the sides directly in this formula? What is the logic behind this? It is a very simple and beautiful concept. The universal rule is, if we triangles in the shape of the triangle? Certainly. If we divide the total angle in a regular polygon with n, we will know how much is an interior angle. According to a source, the only small interior angle in a regular polygon is 60 degrees. Really? 60 degrees?! How is that possible? As a single triangle is the only one with the smallest number of sides, The whole of its outer corners, i.e., sum of exterior angles, will always be 360 degrees. Wait, wait. This is a bit wrong. Since a triangle has three sides, the whole of its outer corners is 360. Okay. But even for the Chilliaguan with 1000 sides that we thought, the whole of its outer corners is 360, right? Won't the rule change if the sides increase? It won't. If we connect this to the bigger picture, if you have made a complete round trip around the shape. You will take a turn near all the roots and come back to the starting point. Hmm, yes. That means, it is like you have made a circle around you, right? A round trip is always 360 degrees. Since the shape you have made is a complete circle, the angles will be 360. For a regular polygon, it is 360 by n,
